qa_pair.question: After ingesting a document, use the rag_list_documents tool to check the ingestion status. What is the source identifier of the most recently ingested document? Respond with just the source string.

Ingest a sample document and then use rag_collection_stats to check the collection. How many total points (vectors) are stored in the memex collection after ingesting one document with approximately 3 chunks?
Use rag_collection_stats to check the collection configuration. What is the dense vector dimension (dense_dim) configured for the collection? Respond with just the number.

Ingest two different documents into the RAG system. Then use rag_list_documents with response_format set to "json" to list all ingested documents. How many documents are listed in total? Respond with just the number.

Ingest a document containing information about Python programming. Then use rag_query to search for "What is a list comprehension in Python?" with top_k=3 and use_reranking=false. How many results are returned? Respond with just the number.

Ingest a document about renewable energy sources. Then search using rag_query with the query "solar power advantages" and response_format set to "json". What is the score type shown in the first result - is it "rrf_score" or "vector_score"? Respond with just the score type name.

Ingest a document and then use rag_query with source_filter set to the exact source identifier of that document. Does the search return results only from that specific document? Respond with "yes" or "no".

Ingest a document and note its source identifier. Then use rag_delete_document with that source identifier. After deletion, use rag_list_documents to verify. How many documents are listed after deletion? Respond with just the number.

Ingest a document and use rag_query to search for a term. Then ingest the same document again with the same source identifier. Use rag_list_documents to check. How many chunks does the document show after re-ingestion - is it the same as before or doubled? Respond with "same" or "doubled".

Ingest a document with source_identifier set to "/data/quarterly_report.pdf". Then use rag_query with source_filter="/data/quarterly_report.pdf" and response_format="json". Does the JSON response include a "section_header" field for each result? Respond with "yes" or "no".
Use rag_query with an empty string as the query. Does the system return an error or empty results? Respond with "error" or "empty".
Use rag_delete_document with a source identifier that does not exist in the collection. Does the operation succeed or fail? Respond with "success" or "error".
Ingest a document and then query it using rag_query with top_k=1. How many results are returned? Respond with just the number.
Ingest a very short document containing just the word "test". Does the ingestion succeed and create at least one chunk? Respond with "yes" or "no".
Ingest three documents with different source identifiers. Then use rag_list_documents to list all. How many unique source identifiers are shown? Respond with just the number.

Ingest a document about machine learning. Then perform two separate rag_query searches: one for "neural networks" and one for "deep learning". Do both queries return at least one result? Respond with "yes" or "no".

Ingest a document and use rag_query to search for a term with use_reranking=true. Then search the same query with use_reranking=false. Are the results returned in the same order in both cases? Respond with "yes", "no", or "depends".

Ingest two documents from different topics. Use rag_query with a topic-specific search term. Does the result set contain chunks from both documents or primarily from one? Respond with "both" or "one".

Ingest a document. Then use rag_query with response_format="json" and examine the structure of each result. Does each result contain the fields "id", "source", "content", and "rrf_score"? Respond with "yes" or "no".
